verdict.line: You lose if you let K'Sante stack two Q hits and poke you down before level 6; you win if you survive to your R and punish his cooldowns.

brief.thesis: K'Sante has the lane and solo-kill edge because Q (Ntofo Strikes) on a 3.5s cooldown lets him poke for free and threaten a pull at 2 stacks, while Volibear has no ranged answer until E (Sky Splitter) unlocks at level 3. The head-to-head still sits near 50% (49.2% over 1,483 games) because Volibear's all-in spikes hard once R (Stormbringer) comes online, turning the lane from a poke fight into a burst check he isn't built to win.

theirWindow.what: The next Q fires a shockwave that pulls you in. Back off or bait it onto a minion instead of standing in the line.

yourWindow.when: His W (Path Maker) is down, 14-10s cooldown
yourWindow.what: Without the dash-stun, K'Sante has no engage or disengage tool besides E. Walk up and force the trade with Q (Thundering Smash) into the stun.

start.why: Most-picked start at 74.2% (48.6% WR over 1,301 games) — the extra sustain and mana regen let you tank Q poke without being forced off the lane before level 3.

boots.why: 50.1% WR over 633 games. K'Sante's whole early kit is auto-attacks and Q pokes — the flat damage reduction blunts his poke and his Attack-marked follow-ups from Passive (Dauntless Instinct).

core.why: Highest-winrate path (59.4% over 101 games) starting here — gives the on-hit tempo Volibear's W (Frenzied Maul) double-tap needs to win trades.
Second item on that same 59.4% path — attack speed scales your Passive (The Relentless Storm) bonus magic damage proc.
Closes out the strongest measured core — the healing amp stacks with W's self-heal to win extended trades against K'Sante's shields.

situational.when: you are already ahead and want more sustain and poke to close the lane out
K'Sante is building tanky and his All Out all-ins are outlasting your burst
you need wave clear and poke damage over committing to all-in trades

runes.keystoneWhy: Highest-picked page (22.7% pick, 50.7% WR) — the ramping attack speed rewards exactly the extended W (Frenzied Maul) double-tap trades you need to out-sustain his Q poke.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is both the most-picked (64.6%) and highest-winrate (49.5%) combo in this matchup — Ignite is critical because it denies the healing K'Sante gets from R (All Out), turning his all-in window into a race you can win.

playing.title: Track his Q stacks, not just his position
playing.detail: Ntofo Strikes (Q, 3.5s cooldown) grants a stack on hit, and at 2 stacks fires a pulling shockwave. Never stand in his short-line Q range once he's at 1 stack.

playing.title: Trade only when you can double-tap W
playing.detail: Frenzied Maul (W, 5s cooldown) marks on first cast and heals you on the second. Commit to trades where you can land both casts, not single pokes.

playing.title: Use E to extend trades past his dash range
playing.detail: Sky Splitter (E, 16s cooldown, 1200 range) slows and shields you if you stand in the blast — throw it to zone him off before he closes with Footwork.

playing.title: All-in the moment R is up at level 6
playing.detail: Stormbringer (R, 160/135/110/110/110s cooldown) leaps in, slows, and grants bonus health — land it then chain Q (Thundering Smash) stun into W for the kill.

playing.title: Respect the All Out burst, don't out-trade it
playing.detail: Once K'Sante's R triggers All Out, his damage, healing, and abilities transform. Disengage or burst him before the transform ramps rather than standing in extended trades.

playing.title: Save Ignite for his all-in, not poke damage
playing.detail: Ignite denies the sustain All Out grants him mid-fight. Holding it for his ultimate window is worth more than using it to secure an early poke kill.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, builds, runes, and summoner picks are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the ability mechanics, trade windows, and cooldown-based reads are my own tactical analysis.
